data.narrative:
Avalanche Energy is a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Robin Langtry and Brian Riordan, having raised $80M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tiers to support a reliable peer-median approach—only zero datapoints met the narrow filter criteria—rendering multiples-based triangulation inapplicable at this time.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable valuation technique here. Using the $80M total raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier between Series A and subsequent funding stages yields an implied valuation of $160M. This method reflects observed step-ups in comparable financings within the sector, though reliance on a single methodology introduces model risk.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $136M (low) to $184M (high), with a median point of $160M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression median. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight-fit peer comparables for validation, execution risk specific to frontier-energy technology, and the absence of recent disclosed market comps at equivalent stage and sector positioning. A fuller triangulation would require either narrower-stage peer data or revenue-based methodologies as corroborating approaches.
